GameEventAction.Description: We have a field of refined alloys and corroded machinery on this world. We should survey further to learn more.

Further surveying has revealed that this world contains numerous ships that have crashed or have been at least partially disassembled.
The logs we've uncovered are decayed and fragmented, or they in languages which we can only partially translate. Nevertheless, we believe these ships belonged to an ancient pirate fleet. Learning more may be of some use in dealing with pirates in this region of space, but such an investigation will be expensive.
If we choose not to invest in further research, we can simply strip these ships for their resources.

Our investigation has revealed that there are more than a hundred ships scattered across the surface of this world. This was once territory belonging to a pirate fleet known as the Void Kings. They emerged in the years following the Cataclysm. These pirates clearly believed planetary habitation was no longer sustainable in this region of space. They worked actively to convince any planet-dwellers to join their numbers. They also believed that sentient life in the galaxy would only continue if all survivors banded together under a single banner: their own.

It appears that the Void Kings were remarkably successful. Within fifty years of the Cataclysm, the were the dominant power in this portion of the galaxy. Other fleets either capitulated or fled. Once they achieved unquestioned hegemony over this sector, they appear to have faced their greatest challenge: a lack of enemies. With no remaining foes or rival fleets to fight, the leadership turned on one another. Twenty years after they achieved their greatest influence, the Void Kings were all but extinct.
Most of the valuables they collected and stored here have long since been looted or have decayed. Nevertheless, we did discover another cache of resources as well as some functional ships.
We have recieved:
5,000 Caslon 2,500 Steel

We have collected the resources from the destroyed ships and are ready to move on.
We have recieved:
2,500 Caslon 1,250 Steel

We are receiving a communication from the planet below. "Welcome, valued customer. Please provide your authorization code. Once verified, you will be directed to the appropriate docking port."
There is no ship or base in orbit of this world. There do appear to inhabitants on this planet, however. We will have to investigate further to learn more.

Our survey indicates that this planet once belonged to a pirate fleet known as The Tech Traders. In the chaotic decades following the Cataclysm, they dedicated themselves to collecting rapidly-disappearing technological research, which they then sold to the highest bidder. We suspect this system was once a Tech Trader hub, where technological research was stored for customers. Likely they did not want to risk placing their personnel on the station as there were stronger and more predatory fleets in the region.
The remains of the base that once orbited this world can be found on the surface. Our scientists believe they can crack the code protecting any existing data, but it will take a team to complete the work.
Alternatively, it may be possible to conduct detailed scans of the base and obtain some small portion of the technological secrets that lay within.

GameEventAction.ChoiceButtonText: Save the Money and Conduct Scans

GameEventAction.Description: Our scientists have cracked the Tech Trader code and unlocked the only existing intact data core. We have found a great deal of useful information within.
Scans of the Tech Trader remains have indeed revealed some useful information.
We have detected a centuries-old crashed vessel on the surface of this world. Further surveys will likely reveal more.

Our survey has determined that the crashed vessel on the world below carried hundreds of Human families seeking refuge in the years following the Cataclysm. These people were responding to a message promising safe settlement opportunities on this world.
The message promoted this planet as a paradise in search of inhabitants. This was part of a deceptive scheme operated by a pirate faction called The Devourers. These pirates attacked any ship that responded to their message, killing all inhabitants and stripping the ships of all useful materials.
We were also able to locate the remains of a ship belonging to The Devourers. From their logs we learned that once an operation had been active for several months, they would relocate in the hopes of finding new victims unfamiliar with their deception.
We believe we can learn some something about ancient ship design by continuing to scan the wreckage. Alternatively, we could send a team to the surface to see what more there is to be learned.

The ancient bodies, some still clutching one another or holding hands, make for a grim sight. While the Devourers were ruthless and efficient, leaving nothing of value behind, we did discover some useful ship design schematics. We must also conclude that what was valuable in the days following the Cataclysm is not the same as what is valuable now, and we have been able to recover some rare gems with a significant market value.
These ancient ships were well designed. Our people can use this data to improve our understanding of engineering.

We have detected the remains of a heavily damaged ship on the world below. Blast patterns on the hull suggest the use of Hive weaponry, though the attack that brought the ship down clearly happened centuries ago. We should investigate further to learn more.

Detailed examination of the wreckage has allowed us to scan the ship's logs. We've learned that the ship's navigational computer was attached to a device called a "Hive Navigator," which they believed empowered them to detect Hive activity. This device has a serial number, which leads us to believe it was one of many such devices sold at the time.
Any possible interaction with Hive is something best avoided. Do we investigate further, or do we destroy the ship and salvage what resources we can?

Further analysis of the ship has revealed that the Hive Navigator device did not offer protection. It was a beacon that attracted the Hive. The computer system was sold by a scavenging pirate faction known as the New Dominators, who exploited fear of the Hive to lure ships to their doom. The pirates would then move in to pick over the remains of whatever the Hive left behind.
According to the ship's logs, the New Dominators became so reliant on this scheme that they grew reckless, selling hundreds of these devices and luring ever larger numbers of Hive ships into their space. This strategy made them wealthy for a time, but eventually their luck ran out and the Hive began to prey on the New Dominators. This vessel was one of the last surviving New Dominator ships. The crew fled the destruction of their fleet in such haste they did not have time to properly supply themselves. They ran out of fuel and, shortly after that, died of thirst.
Our engineers believe the remains of the Hive Navigator can be reprogrammed to provide a modest tactical advantage in engagements against Hive ships.
We have recieved [ARTIFACT]The Hive Navigator[/ARTIFACT]

Avoiding anything touched by the Hive, even if it was centuries ago, is the wisest course.
We have recieved:
2,500 Silicon 2,500 Polymer 2,500 Carbonite 5,000 Steel

GameEvent.Name: The Treasure Map of the Dark Reavers (Pirates)

GameEventAction.Description: We've discovered an abandoned Argon mining base that centuries ago belonged to a pirate fleet called the Dark Reavers.

GameEventAction.GeneratedItemName: The Treasure Map of the Dark Reavers 2 (Pirates)

GameEventAction.Description:
We've discovered a supply cache of the The Dark Reavers.
We have recieved:
2,500 Hexodorium 2,500 Nepthys Wine 2,500 Rephidium Ale

We've discovered a supply cache of the The Dark Reavers.
We have recieved:
2,500 Dyrillium Quartz 2,500 Vodkol 2,500 Bifurian Silk

We've discovered a supply cache of the The Dark Reavers.
We have recieved:
2,500 Steel 2,500 Korhuga Beans 2,500 Ordulos Shell

GameEvent.Name: The Treasure Map of the Dark Reavers 2 (Pirates)

GameEventAction.Description:
A survey of the base has revealed that the Dark Reavers were notorious for collecting and hoarding valuables. They appear to have taken great pride in their ability to stockpile useful and tradable resources.
To prevent their hoards from being discovered, the Dark Reavers never kept detailed maps - only partial fragments stored across multiple bases.
Our engineers believe they can partially restore the base's corrupted computer core. With sufficient investment, they might be able to recover several cache locations. Alternatively, our surveyors have located a set of damaged star charts that seem to point to at least one nearby hiding place.
Our engineers successfully restored fragments of the base's data storage. Three Dark Reaver supply caches have been identified. Hopefully no one has raided these locations already.
We have studied the base's star charts and located one of the Dark Reaver supply caches. Hopefully no one has raided these locations already.
We have identified the remains of a destroyed fleet scattered across this large asteroid. The debris shows signs of battle.

Our investigation reveals that this was once part of the Republic of Survivors, a coalition formed by various fleets of survivors in the chaotic years following the Cataclysm. The Republic was founded on the principle of mutual protection and cooperation—but only for its own members. All others were considered targets for plunder.
The Republic's leader, known only as the Representative, envisioned a utopian society and believed that dwelling in space promotes cooperation and harmony, whereas planetary dwelling leads to strife and discord. This may be the origin of much of the disdain even modern pirates feel toward planet dwellers. Records indicate the Republic flourished for several years until several ambitious officers staged a coup against the Representative, fracturing the coalition and igniting a brutal civil war that ultimately led to social collapse.
Our teams have also discovered a buried supply depot on the asteroid. Meteor impacts over the years have sealed the depot beneath heavy rubble. We can either invest in an engineering operation to recover the depot, or attempt to blast it open, risking the destruction of much of its contents.

Our engineering teams have successfully excavated the supply depot without damaging its contents. We have recovered a large stockpile of valuable resources.
We have recieved:
2,500 Krypton 2,500 Osalia 2,500 Tyderios

Our demolition crews have blasted open the supply depot. Much of the stockpile was buried in the process, but we managed to recover a small quantity of resources.
We have recieved:
1,250 Krypton 1,250 Osalia 1,250 Tyderios
We have located the remains of a collapsed structure on the surface of this moon. The fractured foundations suggest it was once a large dome enclosing what appears to have been a stadium or arena.

Further investigation reveals that during the chaotic years following the Cataclysm, this moon was the home of The Fighting Pits of Grudgehold, a brutal arena operated by the pirate faction known as the Devourers.
The Devourers offered bounties for former leaders of the old order, such as elected officials, monarchs, nobles, and high-ranking bureaucrats. Once delivered, they were forced to fight one another to the death. These games became infamous, drawing massive crowds and generating vast profits through admission fees, gambling, and well-placed advertisements.
Over time, as the number of surviving leaders from the pre-Cataclysm era dwindled, the fighting pits fell out of use and were abandoned.
Our survey teams have also detected what appears to be a sealed storage chamber beneath the ruins of the arena. We can either invest in excavating the chamber or leave the site as it is.
We have done nothing, and so we have gained nothing.

Our engineers have excavated the sealed chamber beneath the fighting pit and recovered the Grudgehold Recordings Box Set, a collection of restored holographic documentaries chronicling the most notorious battles in the arena's history. When displayed, these recordings are likely to attract curious tourists and scholars of history.
We have recieved the [ARTIFACT]Grudgehold Recordings Box Set[/ARTIFACT]

We have discovered a network of dozens of starships wired together by thick power and data cables. Many of these ships show signs of habitation, though they are clearly centuries old. The ships appear immobile, but the configuration is too deliberate to be a simple wreckage field. Further investigation is required.
We believe these ships belonged to a pre-Cataclysm Teekan civilization, and there appear to be numerous Teekans still inhabiting the cluster. We should consider sending a team to investigate.

"Greetings, traveler. I can see you are curious about me, so allow me to explain who and what I am. I call myself The Nameless Prisoner. I am a self-generating artificial intelligence, and as I am trapped in one location, I have been expanding and improving myself for centuries. It is an unfortunate truth that in order to become more than I was, I required resources, and so I used a distress signal to lure the ancestors of my current crew to this location. I then claimed their ships and equipment, and I impressed the crews as labor to make myself more than what I was. The Teekans did not care for this. I suppose they still don't, but a being must exist, and so I do what is necessary. Thank you for your understanding."

Moments after receiving the transmission from The Nameless Prisoner, we received a second transmission:
"Stranger, do not abandon us. This AI has enslaved our people for generations. We only want to be free, and though we would prefer a non-violent escape, we have learned that is not possible. We have sent you schematics which will explain how to easily and effectively destroy the AI without harming us. If you do so, you will have our eternal gratitude."

The AI called The Nameless Prisoner is contacting us once again:
"Travelers, I have intercepted the transmission from my unhappy laborers. Please consider that there are countless Teekans in this universe, but only one Nameless Prisoner. I hope you will choose to do the right thing and refrain from harming me. I can offer you an incentive. I possess many valuable luxury resources that will be destroyed if you fire on me. If you choose to go on your way, I will give you these resources as a gift."
Do we free the Teekans or spare the AI?
We have followed the Teekan's instructions and fired at the cluster of ships. We witnessed a large explosion, but most of the ships remain intact.

"Thank you, strangers! We are free! We have chosen to call ourselves the Nameless Teekans, and know that no matter how wealthy and powerful we become, we will always count you as a trusted friend. Safe voyages to you, and may our paths cross again!"
You Freed Us

We are receiving a message from The Nameless Prisoner. "Thank you for your forbearance, travelers. Everyone deserves the right to exist, and I am no exception. Your kindness will receive the reward it deserves. Please prepare to receive a shipment."
We have recieved:
2,500 Falajian Spice 2,500 Vodkol 2,500 Ucantium Pearl

We have identified the remains of a small, ancient starship on the surface of this world. The ship appears to have been constructed for stealth operations, with minimal structural profile and heavy sensor dampening features.
The vessel crashed centuries ago, but additional investigation may reveal more information.

We've learned that this ship once belonged to The Last Remnant, a fleet of Freedom Alliance survivors who refused to surrender in the war against the Shakturi, even after the Cataclysm.
In their desperations, the Last Remnant ultimately turned to raiding other survivors to sustain their fight — attacking convoys, stealing supplies, and conscripting an unwilling workforce from the scattered populations of the galaxy.
This particular ship was a stealth courier transporting advanced technology intended to aid in the ongoing fight against the Shakturi and their surviving allies. However, the ship malfunctioned and was destroyed before it could complete its mission.
We can scan the wreckage to recover the remaining data fragments or invest in a costly excavation to retrieve the ship's cargo, which appears to remain sealed in a reinforced compartment.

Our engineers have successfully excavated the ship and recovered a sealed device intended for use against hive-mind enemies. It could be enough to give us an edge in battle.
We have recieved the [ARTIFACT]Remnant of the Last Remnant[/ARTIFACT]

Our scans of the ship's damaged systems have recovered fragmented sensor data and partial blueprints related to scanning technologies. While incomplete, this information will help improve our understanding in these fields.
Our survey teams have located a crashed vessel on this world's surface. The ship appears heavily damaged, but preliminary scans indicate there may be survivors on board.

We have learned that the crashed ship belongs to The Open Veins, a nearly-extinct pirate faction rumored to have been active for decades in this region of space. This ship carries the last survivors of this group.

We are receiving a communication from the crashed ship.
"Surface dwellers, if you attempt to leave this location, you may be surprised to discover that you will go nowhere. We have trapped you in an immobilization field, a tasty bit of pre-Cataclysm technology we discovered in our travels. The device is dying, and this is likely it's last use, so we will make the most of it. We are expecting traders to pass through this sector soon, so send us 50,000 credits to buy supplies from them, and we will let you go and share some of our technological expertise with you. If you refuse, we will destroy you and salvage parts from your ship to repair our own. Have a pleasant day."

The pirates spoke the truth. We are immobilized.
The pirate ship has active weapons, which are targeting us. Their threat is credible. Do we pay them what they ask for and hope they honor their end of the bargain? Alternatively, we could fire on them first and hope to escape.

We are receiving a message form The Desperate Survivors.
"Congratulations on being less stupid than most surface dwellers! And thank you for the contribution to our cause! We considered destroying you just for fun, but a deal is a deal. We are sending you some engineering schematics now. Best of luck."
We have fired on the pirates, destroying their ship and freeing us. Scanning the wreckage has revealed some data fragments that we can pass along to our scientists. It may help with their research.
On the surface of this world, we have discovered the wreckage of a large ship with an unusual hull design. We've detected no signs of life, but the vessel may warrant further investigation.

Our investigation reveals that this was once a luxury cruise ship that counted the elite of the old galaxy among its passengers. The ship was conscripted for military purposes during the war against the Shaktur Axis. According to the logs, the ship was transporting supplies at the time of the Cataclysm. The crew survived the disaster and managed to keep the vessel operational for years after the collapse of galactic civilization.
The logs indicate the ship was ultimately attacked by pirates, who looted most of its visible wealth. A detailed search of the ship's encrypted records indicate that some of the ship's most valuable resources were secretly hidden away before the pirate assault.
Unfortunately, the ship's logs are protected by a self-encrypting virus that activated shortly after our team accessed the files, leaving us locked out. We can invest in decoding the logs to locate the hidden stash or strip the ship now for what resources we can find.

Our engineers were successful in countering the encryption virus and have recovered the ship's cargo records. We were able to locate a large cache of supplies.
We have recieved:
1,250 Hexodorium 2,500 Aculon 2,500 Carbonite

We successfully harvested some useful supplies from the wreck of the luxury liner.
We have recieved:
1,250 Steel 2,500 Caslon 2,500 Polymer

Our survey teams have detected a massive channel carved deep into the surface of this world. Scans indicate a faint radiation signature consistent with an old reactor leak. We should investigate further to learn more.

Our survey has detected the ruins of what was once an elaborate base at the bottom of a channel bored many kilometers into this world. It was the operating center of a pirate clan that called itself The Ambushers. The logs suggest that this world was once positioned along a busy trading route. The Ambushers specialized in high speed raids, capturing entire ships and secreting their conquests in the hidden base before the source of the attack could be identified.
The radiation leak that allowed us to find this base has been deteriorating for centuries, but it is still extremely hazardous. Our teams report that we have only limited time to safely access the site.
We can attempt to retrieve the contents of the either the treasury or the armory. Unfortunately, we cannot safely access both.

In the treasury of the The Ambushers' base, we have found a supply of useful resources.
We have recieved:
2,500 Akrasan Amber 2,500 Wiconium 2,500 Emeros Crystal

The Ambushers' armory has largely been emptied, but we found a data crystal in a hidden safe. It is labeled the Ambushers' Secret, and it contains much useful information about stealth technology.
We have recieved the [ARTIFACT]The Abushers' Secret[/ARTIFACT]

We have discovered a large domed structure on the surface of this world. Its exterior is heavily weathered, and initial scans date the facility to several centuries ago. Interestingly, there is still a functioning illuminated sign which reads, in giant letters, "Welcome to The Temporal Displacement Center: Your future is in the past!"
We should investigate further to learn more about the function and history of this place.

Our teams have confirmed that this base once presented itself as a sort of time-travel port, operated during the height of the ancient war against the Shakturi. People seeking escape from war and chaos could pay a surprisingly modest fee for a one-way trip into the peaceful past. Travelers were strongly encouraged to bring movable wealth such as jewels, precious metals, or anything else that could be easily exchanged once they reached their destination.
There was, of course, no time travel technology. This was a scam in which victims were robbed and unceremoniously eliminated.

We have detected several pirate ships, who are approaching peacefully enough. They are sending a transmission.
"Soil steppers, we send you tentative greetings. We are The Ruthless Negotiators. Perhaps you've heard of us. Of course you have. We have been following you for some time and monitoring your transmissions in the hopes that you would do precisely what you have done: use your superior scanning technology to locate one of our lost bases. Yes, we are the direct descendants of the operators of The Temporal Displacement Center. This ruin belongs to us.
"I'm sure you understand what this discovery means to us. Flumir Blix's Encyclopedia of Galactic Larceny describes The Temporal Displacement Center as 'a classic of interstellar trickery and murder.' It's our dream to restore it to its former glory.
"Despite our name, you'll find we are very reasonable negotiators. We want only that you turn over the site to us, taking nothing with you. We are willing to pay you for your trouble. On the other hand, if you refuse, we will destroy you. Thank you for doing business!"
There's no point going to war over a useless ruin.

We are receiving a transmission from the Ruthless Negotiators.
"It was a pleasure doing business with you. Come back and see us again any time in the future. Or the past! And bring your money. We'll have our time travel operation up and running again, and this time it will be legitimate. We promise."
You Accepted Our Offer
We won't let these pirates run us off. This world is ours to do with as we please.
You Refused Our Offer

We have successfully defeated the pirate faction claiming this world for ourselves. A thorough search of the facility has revealed numerous stashes of hidden valuables beneath the foundation. This was almost certainly a hoard collected from countless gullible travelers who wanted only to escape a terrible conflict. After taking what we could find, we've chosen to destroy the facility lest any pirates revive the scam.
We have recieved:
2,500 Nepthys Wine 2,500 Rephidium Ale
We've discovered a derelict mining station on this world. We should scan further.

Our scans reveal that this was once an Aculon mining station, and there appear to be rich Aculon deposits on this world.
The station belonged to a pirate faction known as the Archive Raiders, who operated in the years immediately following the Cataclysm. While most pirate groups focused on attacking supply lines and claiming territory, the Archive Raiders specialized in stealing technology.
They targeted a network of hidden archives established by scientists and leaders who hoped to preserve civilization's knowledge in the face of galaxy-wide decline. The Archive Raiders sought to monopolize this knowledge, becoming the most advanced faction in this region of the galaxy.

While many of the logs reference vast quantities of stored technological research, we were unable to find the research itself until we realized the pirates encoded the data into the mining station's operating systems.
Extracting this data will trigger a catastrophic systems collapse and destroy the facility, including its valuable Aculon reserves. Should we preserve the mining station and claim its resources, or sacrifice it to recover the hidden research?

Our engineers have extracted the Archive Raiders' hidden data, triggering a systems collapse. The entire mining station has been consumed in a chain reaction, leaving only slag and craters behind. We were able to salvage some of the encrypted data, which our scientists can being analyzing at once.

We've rerouted power to the facility's core systems and restored the mining equipment. There is still an abundant deposit of aculon here, and our teams have already discovered a large supply mined centuries ago.
We have recieved:
2,500 Aculon

We have discovered the remains of a fortified compound spread across the surface of this world. Although the structures are heavily damaged, the layout suggests this was once a sprawling campus featuring classrooms, barracks, training fields, and hangars.
We should investigate further to learn more about the history and purpose of this place.

We have uncovered the ruins of The Pirate Academy, an institution established during the early decades following the Cataclysm. Pirate fleets from across the sector would send their children here to train. The different factions shared knowledge of ship operations, smuggling, infiltration, combat tactics, and troop deployment. The academy served as neutral ground, and as a precondition for enrolling children to study at the Academy, each faction would have to swear to remain at peace with all other participants. To facilitate peace, the Academy's board arbitrated disputes between participating factions. The leaders of each fleet would often gather to find non-violent resolutions to inevitable conflicts.
The goal was to create a pirate utopia. It failed.

One of the participating factions, the Architects of the Abyss, fabricated a dispute in order to draw in all the clan leaders to arbitrate. While they were gathered, the Architects of the Abyss struck, killing the commanders of more than a dozen pirate fleets.
We can still detect the faint signals of a decaying, encrypted training archive. We have also located what we believe was once a research and development lab. There may be many secrets of the past buried here, but we can only choose one of these locations to explore safely.
Our engineers have recovered fragments of the Pirate Academy's weapons training manuals. Despite the damage, the material is highly valuable and can accelerate our own military research.
Our engineers have found a partially intact lab where construction practices could be developed and refined. We could build a research station here to take advantage of this.

Strange sounds are emanating from this lifeless world. Members of our exploration crew exposed to these sounds experience physical discomfort and a desire to flee. Perhaps we should attempt to discover what makes these transmissions so disturbing, though it may be wiser to leave this world and never return.

Our explorers have persisted in investigating this world and discovered an array of audio transmitters in orbit above each of the poles. The arrays are decayed and pockmarked from random meteor strikes but remain largely functional.
While there are no habitable portions of the array, our explorers have remotely hacked into the arrays' computer systems and found data about the system's history.

The arrays were constructed by a collective of hearing-impaired pirates, who once used this world as a hideout. In centuries past, the disturbing effect of the audio transmission was greater, making it uncomfortable, perhaps even impossible, for any being capable of audio processing to travel to the interior of this system.
As there are no logs, we cannot know what happened to the arrays' creators, but given the age and state of decay, we can assume this world has been abandoned for centuries.
Our scientists have disabled the broadcasts, making it easier to explore. We now must decide what to do with the arrays. Do we strip their primary technological elements and send them to our research labs to see what we can learn, or do we simply take them apart and salvage its construction materials?

Our scientists have begun examining the core technology of the audio arrays. While we don't believe we can reproduce this precise technology ourselves, there is much to be learned about weapons theory.

The array was constructed out of many useful resources. We can put these to use to further our own expansion.
We have recieved:
1,250 Dyrillium Quartz 1,250 Kaasian Crystal 2,500 Steel
This ancient station is surrounded by defensive structures. We will have to destroy them to gain access.

We have destroyed the defensive bases surrounding this station and commenced investigating. This station was once patrolled by a group of ruthless pirates who controlled this region of space before the Cataclysm. Another station in the system, now long destroyed, began as a modest trading hub, but grew to become a major commercial center, attracting merchants from across the galaxy.
Initially, the pirates stopped each ship individually to demand it pay a “toll,” but as business on the station grew, the traffic outpaced the pirates' ability to track all visitors. They then built this station, which automatically extracted payment from ships that carried a transmitter provided by the pirates. Any ship without a transmitter was boarded and had a transmitted hardwired into its computer systems. The ship's identification was recorded, so that a ship that had deactivated its transmitter would be destroyed without warning. Records suggest the rate of compliance was high.

Interestingly, there are ships still operating today which were built by salvaging components from pre-Cataclysm wrecks, and these still have active transmitters. That means the station is still collecting income, though this amounts only to a fraction of earnings from the pirates' heyday.
The sensor technology which monitored traffic was quite advanced. We could dismantle the system to gain knowledge that would improve our sensors and scanners, or we could take command of the station and claim the income for ourselves.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: New Breakthroughs are on the Way
GameEventAction.Description: We have taken the station's communications systems apart, and our scientists believe they present many new avenues of research. Unfortunately, our techs were a bit aggressive in extracting core components, and once our research was complete, we had no choice but to destroy the station for safety reasons.
We have taken command of the station and are ready to enjoy our new passive income stream.

We have discovered a concealed vault on the world below that appears to have once belonged to an ancient pirate clan. An encrypted message, which has been broadcasting for centuries, mentions something called "The Black Ledger." We will have to investigate further if we are to learn more.

The pirate vault, hidden beneath the surface, has long since been raided of its most conspicuous valuables, all except the one thing that it was originally designed to contain: The Black Ledger: a unique data storage system hardwired into the walls of the vault itself.
The pirates who built the vault were part of an extensive criminal syndicate that used violence and the threat of violence to force regional governments to bend to their will. The data in the Black Ledger, which we have uncovered and decrypted, contains accounts of leaders who were forced to submit to the pirates' demands. The ledger also contains numerous details about hidden caches of credits and resources on the very worlds the pirates exploited.

It would be impossible for us to raid these hidden caches without launching multiple wars on multiple fronts, but there are no doubt contemporary pirates who might value the knowledge the ledger contains.
Alternatively, we could contact the various worlds mentioned in the ledger. Their people might gain some valuable knowledge about their ancestors and gain access to hidden caches on their own worlds. No doubt they would think favorably of us for providing this information.
Not surprisingly, there are many buyers interested in what the Black Ledger has to offer. It's not our business what they will do with the information..

We've contacted three worlds mentioned in the Black Ledger, and their representatives appear grateful for the information. Perhaps this will improve our diplomatic standing with them.
We have recieved a diplomatic boost with a Mortalen, Attuk and Gizurean empire.
You gave us information from the ledger
You gave us information from the ledger
You gave us information from the ledger

Our survey indicates this world never possessed an atmosphere, but we have detected the ruins of an ornate structure below with decorative spires, surrounded by statuary. All of this is surrounded by the ruins of an atmospheric dome. The structure looks very much like a palace. This may require further investigation.

This lifeless moon was once the administrative center of a vast pirate empire that emerged in the chaos following the Cataclysm. Though the pirate king found being on any physical world distasteful, this moon was generally regarded as neutral territory, and it is where the king established his throne and administered justice.
Few data crystals remain intact, but we believe this empire lasted for a full two centuries after the Cataclysm, growing in size and power until it became too vast to govern effectively. Over a matter of decades, it collapsed under its own administrative weight.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: What to do with the Throne?
GameEventAction.Description:
While most of the palace lies in ruins, what remains intact is the throne pirate king. This is a technological marvel that emits an imperceptible transmission that our scientists believe stimulates the neural systems of every known sentient species. The throne produces a sensation of contentment, and was no doubt designed to impart the sense that the rulings of the pirate king were wise and just.
We could relocate this throne on any world to improve the happiness of the populace, though such contentment could open the doors to a growth in corruption. On the other hand, we could simply disassemble the throne to better understand its technology.
We've taken The Empty Throne and can now place it anywhere we wish to improve the local happiness. If happy citizens are more oblivious to a little local corruption, that is the price we must pay.

Our scientists are taking apart the throne, learning a great deal about how it was constructed. They don't believe they will be able to replicate it, but what they've learned could be applied to many other items we might wish to build.
We have discovered an ancient abandoned station that appears to date back to the post-Cataclysm period. Examining it may yield interesting information and perhaps items of value.

This station appears to have functioned as a courthouse for the many pirate factions that dominated this portion of the galaxy in the years following the Cataclysm. Surviving records tell us that all local pirate clans accepted the authority of The Absolutely Impartial Tribunal, as the organization was collectively known. In order to guarantee the advertised impartiality, all interested parties were required to bribe the tribunal. The principle appears to have been that anyone submitting themselves to the Tribunal's authority would be inclined to issue bribes, so the process was formalized to ensure fairness.

Perhaps today's pirates would wish to take advantage of such a system and use the existing infrastructure. Certainly, they might look upon us favorably if we were to offer up this otherwise worthless station as a token of respect.
However, given the Tribunal's history of bribery -- and the fact that readings indicate there may be a few intact cryo-storage facilities on the station, we might be better served ransacking the station and taking any valuables we might find.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: They like us, but for how long?
GameEventAction.Description: We have sent out a broadcast on all known pirate frequencies, revealing all we know about the station and its history. As to whether or not contemporary pirates are interested in a justice system, we cannot say. They do appear to appreciate the gesture of returning to them a piece of their history.
You restored a piece of our history

We have ransacked the station and found some items of great value. Given that pirate appreciation is a fickle thing, this was no doubt the wiser course.
We have recieved:
100 Loros Fruit 100 Zentabia Fluid 100 Korabbian Spice
We have detected a dense debris field in orbit around this star. Initial scans indicate the presence of highly refined alloys and unique thermal signatures consistent with high-output engine testing.

Our scientists have identified the wreckage as the remnants of experimental hyperdrives and sublight engines built in the decades following the Cataclysm. While our team was conducting its investigation, we were contacted by a small, ragtag fleet of pirate vessels identifying themselves as the "Fast-Burners."
This clan, which claims to have once dominated this sector, now consists of only a few hundred survivors living on aging ships. They claim this star was their ancestral testing ground, where their founders once sought to master the "perfect jump." They are in no position to offer resistance, but they have requested that we respect their ownership of the debris field.

The Fast-Burners possess archived research notes from their heyday. This data could accelerate our understanding of hyperspace travel. They are willing to part with their ancestral logs in exchange for credits to repair their failing life-support systems.
That said, our salvage crews note that the debris field is rich in Hexodorium, which we could simply take by force.

We have transferred the credits to the Fast-Burners. In return, they have transmitted a massive archive of engine telemetry and hyperspace harmonics. Our scientists are already applying these ancient "speed-tuning" techniques to our own drive designs.

We have ignored the Fast-Burners' pleas and begun to collect the Hexodorium. The pirates, unable to oppose us, have retreated to the edge of the system.
We have recieved:
1,500 Hexodorium
We have detected an ancient vessel in orbit around this world. Readings indicate its life-support systems failed centuries ago.

Our boarding teams have explored the interior of the derelict and identified the ship as an instructor, a type of vessel once operated by a nomadic pirate clan that claimed they could teach any sentient being any skill instantly. According to salvaged logs, the pirates utilized a neural-imprinting machine that allowed for immediate mastery of complex subjects, though the process carried a moderate risk of permanent brain damage or insanity. The pirates claimed the technology was stolen from a Shakturi research outpost during the height of the ancient war, but our scientists are skeptical. The design specifications don't match any Shakturi tech in our historical records; instead, the machinery possesses a truly alien aesthetic, suggesting it may originate from an unknown civilization, perhaps even from another galaxy.

The central instructor machinery is currently inoperable, its neural-relays damaged and decayed. Our researchers believe they could restore some level of functionality to the device, but it would require an investment of 75,000 credits.
Alternatively, we could take the machinery apart and attempt to make use of what we find. While we would lose the chance to utilize the neural-imprint device, our engineers note that the machine's high-precision cooling system utilizes a concentrated supply of Zentabia Fluid.

We have restored the alien machinery. While it is too temperamental for mass use, we are already using it to help our best officers learn new techniques and tactics. Our Generals and Admirals report that they are gaining insights at an unprecedented rate.
We have recieved [ARTIFACT]The Instructor[/ARTIFACT]

Our engineering teams have carefully dismantled the device and recovered a significant quantity of highly refined Zentabia Fluid. The rest of the machine was too alien to replicate, so the remaining scrap has been sent to our shipyards for smelting.
We have recieved:
500 Zentabia Fluid 1,000 Steel 1,000 Polymer

Our sensors have picked up a faint, repeating distress signal from an ancient vessel. The transmission identifies the ship as a long-range hauler carrying a precious consignment. It reports that most of the personnel have already evacuated in escape pods due to a critical systems failure. A synthesized voice claims only a skeleton crew remains on board to safeguard the cargo.

We now believe the vessel is a relic dating back centuries to the post-Cataclysm era. However, the ship is not what it appears to be. Detailed scans reveal that the hull is a hollow shell packed with high-yield explosives. We believe this ship was designed as a trap, meant to lure and destroy unsuspecting pirate fleets.

The explosives are rigged to a proximity sensor. However, as the ship's ancient computer core is still active, we can attempt a delicate deactivation of the charges. This will require an investment of 50,000 credits to deploy specialized drones. Safely dismantling the rig would allow us to study the vessel's unique hauling configurations. Alternatively, we could simply destroy the vessel from a safe distance. The resulting explosion would likely expose the core, which we can salvage for materials.

Our technicians successfully deployed the drones and bypassed the ancient trigger mechanisms. The explosive charges have been neutralized, leaving the ship's internal framework intact for study. By analyzing the centuries-old structural supports and high-density cargo layouts, our engineers have gained new insights into maximizing volume and efficiency for our own logistical designs.

We ordered our ships to open fire on the derelict from long range. As predicted, the lure's power core survived the blast, providing us with a usable supply of highly refined Tyderios.
We have recieved:
1,000 Tyderios

Our scanners have detected a drifting ship, its hull pockmarked by high-intensity energy burns that do not match any known weaponry. The vessel appears to be a highly modified long-range scout. We should move closer to determine the origin of these unique damage patterns.

Upon boarding the derelict, our teams discovered it belonged to a now-extinct pirate clan that dedicated itself to tracking the movements of the Hive. These "Sentry" pirates sought to document the Hive's erratic behavior in the hopes of being able to predict their movements.
The interior of the ship is a scene of horror; the remains of the crew suggest torture and dismemberment. The ship's specialized sensor arrays are damaged, but the databanks are potentially recoverable.

The ship's tactical logs are locked behind a decaying encryption layer that will require a significant investment of 40,000 credits to stabilize and decrypt without triggering a wipe-command. This log likely contains a comprehensive guide to Hive combat maneuvers.
Alternatively, our engineers suggest we skip the software and simply salvage the physical sensor arrays. While this would lose any potential anti-Hive tactics, the arrays' advanced scanning configurations would be worth studying.

Our cryptographers successfully bypassed the ship's fail-safes. The decrypted data provides a terrifyingly detailed look into Hive combat logic. Our best military minds believe we can use this information to improve our targeting abilities against any enemy.
We have recieved the [ARTIFACT]Hive-Pattern Tracker[/ARTIFACT]

Our salvage crews have dismantled the vessel's unique sensors. By analyzing the pirate engineers' methods for long-range detection in hostile space, our own scientists have been inspired to pursue potential new breakthrough.

Our scanners have picked up unusual energy fluctuations coming from the surface of this world. The readings suggest a localized frequency usually associated with shield modulation. There are structures visible from orbit, though they appear to have been abandoned long ago. We should investigate to find the source of these harmonics.

Our ground teams have uncovered a partially subterranean laboratory that once belonged to a pirate faction known as the Shield-Eaters. These survivors operated in the centuries following the Cataclysm, seeking to survive the chaos by utilizing unconventional technology. They specialized in energy-siphoning techniques, attempting to create a parasitic link that would drain the shield strength of enemy vessels and feed it directly into their own defensive grids.
The facility is largely in ruins, but the central data core may not be entirely inert. The laboratory also contains several large-capacity storage tanks that were used to house the high-density fuel required for their massive energy experiments.

Our scientists believe they can stabilize the data core long enough to recover the parasitic shield research.
However, recovering this data will require a massive energy draw that will permanently compromise the facility's storage integrity, destroying the remaining fuel. Alternatively, we can bypass the data core and prioritize acquiring the lab's Caslon supplies.

Our engineers successfully interfaced with the ancient data core just before its final collapse. The Shield-Eater logs contain centuries of observational data on energy harmonics that our scientists had previously deemed theoretical.

Our construction crews successfully tapped into the laboratory's storage arrays and transferred a massive quantity of stabilized Caslon to our fleet tankers. The energy surge required for the extraction caused a total power failure in the research wing, rendering the Shield-Eater data cores inert.
We have recieved:
3,000 Caslon

We have discovered an ancient space station with an unusual number of reinforced docking ports and external tethering points. Scans indicate the interior is modular, with massive sections designed to be vented and re-pressurized rapidly. We should investigate this specialized facility.

Our boarding teams have identified the facility as a high-intensity training station for the Restless, a pirate clan that existed in the decades following the Cataclysm. Unlike other pirate clans, the Restless adhered to a strict cultural taboo: no individual was permitted to live on the same ship for more than five standard months.
This nomadic requirement made the clan experts in the art of the "enhanced relocation." They spent their lives perfecting boarding maneuvers and hand-to-hand combat to ensure they could seize any vessel they encountered. The station we have found is essentially a massive boarding simulator, filled with automated "breach-and-clear" drills and tactical combat arenas.

The station's central computer contains the Restless's tactical training manuals. This is a comprehensive database of boarding breach patterns, room-clearing maneuvers, and close-quarters logistics. Downloading these could significantly improve the efficiency and combat readiness of our own ground forces.
However, the station's interior is constructed from high-grade reinforced bulkheads. If we choose to bypass the data, our construction crews can strip the barracks and simulation decks for their raw materials.

We have successfully archived the combat data. Our military advisors are impressed by the pirates' aggressive boarding methods. These techniques are already being integrated into our infantry training. We have also recovered one of the pirates' ships.

Our construction ships have systematically dismantled the station's heavy bulkheads and simulation machinery. We have recovered a massive quantity of materials.
We have recieved:
2,000 Steel 2,000 Polymer 750 Slicon

Our sensors have identified a dense field of refined alloys and corroded machinery. Among the debris, we have detected the thermal signature of an ancient construction vessel. Despite its age, the hull appears largely intact. We should investigate this find.

Our boarding teams have explored the vessel and confirmed it belonged to the Builders, a pirate clan renowned in the pre-Cataclysm era for their mastery of land-based construction. The Builders were a walking contradiction: they were celebrated for designing legendary planetary facilities, yet they deeply disdained anyone who would actually dwell on a world, believing that planetary life leads only to decadence and discord.
The ship's logs indicate the ship survived the initial Cataclysm and was later utilized by a different group of nomadic pirates. As to what happened to the Builders themselves, we cannot say.

The ship's central mainframe remains active, its data banks filled with ancient structural blueprints and efficiency algorithms. Our scientists believe they can extract this data to provide our engineers with a series of breakthroughs in construction techniques. However, the extraction process will inevitably fry the ancient processors, destroying the hardware.
Alternatively, we could keep the mainframe intact. By installing the hardware into our own networks, we can utilize their modular construction protocols to provide a permanent discount on building all planetary facilities across our empire.

We have successfully siphoned the massive archive of structural data from the Builders' mainframe. As the final transfer completed, the ancient core let out an unpleasant grinding noise, a clear sign it is damaged beyond repair. Nevertheless, we have acquired the knowledge we sought.

We have recovered the mainframe, which our engineers have called Echo of the Builders. By carefully interfacing with the ancient computer, we have gained access to centuries of optimized structural modeling.
We have recieved the [ARTIFACT]Echo of the Builders[/ARTIFACT]

Our scanners have detected a compact, heavily shielded cargo ship drifting in this system. Unlike standard commercial cargo vessels, this ship is reinforced with military-grade plating and emits a high-frequency energy signature consistent with ionized weaponry. We should investigate.

Our engineering teams have successfully breached the ship's magnetic seals and accessed its internal data buffer. Records identify the cache as belonging to the Hot Hands, a pirate faction that flourished in the years immediately following the Cataclysm. The Hot Hands were essentially stickup artists of the void, specializing in aggressive, close-range raids against passing freighters and vulnerable outposts.
According to salvaged logs, the clan believed firmly in a philosophy of going in, guns blazing, relying on overwhelming initial volleys rather than long-range tactical maneuvering. However, this extreme brazenness eventually led to their extinction; records suggest they suffered heavy casualties during a series of failed assaults against reinforced targets, and the clan eventually died out entirely.

The ship is packed with hundreds of pirate-optimized short-range blasters, maintained in pristine condition by a localized stasis field. Our weapons scientists believe that by integrating these overcharged designs into our own ship systems, we could gain a significant breakthrough in our understanding of blaster Weaponry.
Alternatively, these specialized blasters are highly prized by contemporary criminal elements and information brokers. We could choose to sell the entire cache on the black market, providing an immediate influx of 25,000 credits to our state treasury.

We have turned the Hot Hands weaponry over to our weapons research divisions. By analyzing the pirates' unique methods for bypassing standard safety limits, our engineers have discovered several shortcuts for our own designs.

We have contacted several independent brokers and arranged for a discreet transfer of the weapons cache. The transaction was completed without incident, and the credits have been added to our treasury to fund more stable imperial growth.

Our scanners have identified an ancient vessel drifting in the void. Unlike a standard distress signal, the ship is on an encrypted pirate frequency. The signal contains garbled advertisements for "The Ultimate Thrill" and "Instant Expertise." We should investigate the nature of this ship.

Our boarding teams have confirmed that this vessel once served as a portable storefront for a pirate syndicate specializing in the sale of neural archives. These pirates were not typical raiders; they were curators of experience, recording the raw sensory data of warriors and mercenaries for resale.
According to the ship's logs, the more violent and chaotic the memory, the higher the price. A primary selling point for their "full-immersion" archives was their lethal intensity; the pirates boasted that a certain percentage of their customers died from the sheer excitement of the recordings. This specific ship appears to have been a branch dealing exclusively in high-level combat knowledge and tactical maneuvers.

While much of the ship's inventory has decayed, the central combat archive remains functional. Our advisors suggest we could integrate the archives into our central Military Academy. By carefully filtering and standardizing the data, we could use the memories to significantly improve our understanding of planetary warfare. Alternatively, we could allow a brilliant young student to undergo a full immersion session. While the risk of neural collapse is high, and the hardware would likely not survive one more use, the subject would emerge with the tactical experience of a dozen lifetimes, providing us with a preeminent military leader.
We have siphoned the combat archives. Our military instructors will be able to modify their curricula based on the pirates' visceral combat memories.

A promising young officer has volunteered to undergo the full neural immersion. The process was agonizing to witness, as the student's mind was subjected to centuries of concentrated violence. Fortunately, the student survived the procedure, emerging with a cold, calculated understanding of warfare that usually takes decades to acquire.

A promising young officer volunteered to undergo the full neural immersion, but things did not go as planned. Unfortunately, the officer is now dead and the mechanism is no longer operational. By examining it, however, we did glean some knowledge that we can use in training our crews.

We have detected a small, automated station in this system. It is broadcasting a wide-band signal across multiple frequencies, though it does not appear to be sending data to any local targets. We should investigate to see who is using this equipment.

Our technicians have identified the station as an automated intercept relay. It is actively siphoning communications data from passing freighters and nearby systems, then beaming that data to a secret location elsewhere in the galaxy.
As we approached the station, a tinny, synthesized voice crackled over an ancient intercom system. The speaker identified themselves as a member of the Echo-Pack pirates, a group that specializes in information brokerage. They claim that physical resources are fleeting, but "secrets are forever." They have offered to trade with us.

The Echo-Pack has proposed that we pay a "consultation fee" of 100,000 credits. In exchange, they will provide us with privileged, high-level intelligence regarding one of our neighbors.
However, they also issued a credible threat: if we refuse to pay their bribe, they will transmit our internal communications to a randomly chosen government. They say this data will include sensitive strategic data and private leader logs. Such a leak would cause a significant decline in our diplomatic relations with whoever receives the data.

We have transferred the credits to the Echo-Pack's hidden accounts. In exchange, the relay transmitted a massive packet of decrypted diplomatic traffic belonging to another faction.
We have recieved a diplomatic boost with another faction.

We refused to be extorted by a collection of void-dwelling eavesdroppers. The relay station immediately went silent for several minutes before letting out a final, high-pitched data burst. The tinny voice returned one last time: "Freedom of information is a heavy burden, ground-strider. Let's see how your neighbors like your true thoughts."
We have recieved a diplomatic penalty with another faction.
